desc:
A binary tree is full if every node has either zero or two children. No node may have exactly one child. Return true if the given tree is full and false otherwise. The empty tree is full.

How trees are given. There is no tree type here. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level-order (top to bottom, left to right), the same way LeetCode serialises trees. A missing child is written as -1, and every real node value is non-negative. The children of a missing node are not listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped, so a non-empty array never ends with -1. The empty tree is [].

For example, [1, 2, 3, -1, 4] describes the tree on the left: the root is 1 with children 2 and 3, node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child, and node 3 is a leaf.

    1
   / \
  2   3
   \
    4

For tree = [1, 2, 3, -1, -1, 4, 5] the answer is true: node 1 has children 2 and 3, node 2 is a leaf, and node 3 has children 4 and 5. For tree = [1, 2, 3, 4] it is false, because node 2 has only a left child (4).
constraints: Every tree array follows the encoding above exactly (valid level-order, no trailing -1)
hints: Look at one node at a time. Which combinations of 'has a left child' and 'has a right child' are allowed?
Only 'none' and 'both' are allowed, so a node is bad exactly when its two child slots disagree: one is missing and the other is a real node.
Visit every node (stack, queue or recursion) and return false at the first node with exactly one child. If none exists, return true.
editorial: The condition is local: it can be checked at every node independently. For each node count its real children; the tree is full exactly when no node has a count of 1. Equivalently, (left is missing) == (right is missing) must hold at every node.

In the level-order encoding you can do this with one scan of the structure: each real node owns two consecutive child slots, and a node is bad when exactly one of its two slots is -1. The work is one visit per node, so O(n) time; no extra structure beyond the traversal stack is needed.
